colleges.name: University of Washington (Seattle)
colleges.wants: UW treats the essay as its chance to meet the person behind grades and numbers. Academic preparation and performance come first in review, alongside personal achievements and traits such as service, leadership, real responsibility and distinctive perspectives. It wants original writing in the applicant's own voice.
colleges.notes: First-year applicants no longer write a UW-specific essay; the required essay is the Common App personal essay. Application route confirmed at https://admit.washington.edu/apply/first-year/how-to-apply/ (UW does not consider recommendation letters, interviews or demonstrated interest). promptsFrom value 'common-app' is a suggested key, not from the page.

colleges.name: Penn State (University Park)
colleges.appliesVia: MyPennState application or Common App (no preference between them)
colleges.wants: Penn State weighs the academic record most heavily: courses, grades and course levels from grades 9-11, plus test scores if submitted. The optional personal statement and activities list can be additional factors, and reviewers consider the roles an applicant fills as student, family member, athlete, volunteer or employee.
colleges.notes: Personal Statement is optional; Common App Essay is accepted as the Personal Statement. No official Penn State essay-advice page was found, so no principles are included. 'No preference' statement seen at https://www.psu.edu/admission/undergraduate/how-to-apply. Pages are live with 2026 dates (Early Action grace period to November 5, 2026).

prompts.text: Some students have a background, identity, interest, or talent that is so meaningful they believe their application would be incomplete without it. If this sounds like you, then please share your story.
prompts.instructions: Required: answer ONE of the seven Common App personal essay prompts. UW states no preference among them. Maximum 650 words; responses under 250 words are not accepted.

rubrics.title: UW Holistic Review factors

criteria.name: Academic achievement
criteria.description: Strong overall academic record, shown through grades and the depth, breadth and rigor of courses. This remains the primary factor.

criteria.name: College-preparatory coursework
criteria.description: Using available advanced options such as AP, IB, Running Start or college in the high school, or going beyond minimum subject requirements. No model is favored.

criteria.name: Senior year
criteria.description: Making full use of the final year of high school.

criteria.name: Service and leadership
criteria.description: Evidence of commitment to community service and to leading others.

criteria.name: Significant responsibility
criteria.description: Carrying real responsibility in family, community, a job or activities.

criteria.name: Overcoming disadvantage
criteria.description: Completing a college-preparatory education despite socio-economic or other disadvantage; considered for Washington state residents only.

rubrics.notes: Live page, footer 2026, no cycle year stated. These are review factors, not an essay scoring rubric; UW publishes no weights or scores.

rubrics.title: Penn State Application Evaluation factors

criteria.name: Academic record
criteria.description: The most important part of review: academic courses taken, grades earned and course levels across grades 9-11.

criteria.name: Test scores
criteria.description: SAT or ACT scores are considered only if the applicant chooses to provide them; there is no minimum GPA or score.

criteria.name: Additional factors
criteria.description: May include the personal statement and activities list, and for some programs an audition or portfolio review.

criteria.name: Roles and experiences
criteria.description: Reviewers look at the roles an applicant holds, such as student, sibling, athlete, volunteer or employee, to build a class with varied interests.

rubrics.notes: Live page, footer 2026, no cycle year stated. General review factors, not an essay rubric. Page also says recommendation letters are not used (steps-to-apply page).

principles.text: Treat the essay seriously: write in formal, standard English rather than the casual style of a text message.
Tell a personal story in your own individual voice; many of the strongest statements take that form.
Keep the writing concise and straightforward, and proofread it repeatedly before submitting.
The writing must be your own original work; any review by a person or AI tool has to be responsible and ethical.
